editor.rules: When and where it is shown
editor.linkHint: https only. Used by the QR and the {{name}} variable.
editor.showQr: Show a QR of the link
editor.imageHint: An https address or a site path, for example /brand/logo.png. If there is an image it replaces the icon.
editor.variables: Variables you can use in the texts: {{vars}}.
editor.englishFallback: If you leave the English empty, the Spanish text is used.
editor.priorityHint: 0 to 100. A higher priority goes first in the queue.
editor.weightHint: 0 to 100. Among pieces with the same priority, more weight shows up more often; 0 = never.
editor.datesHint: Empty = no limit. Dates use your local time.
editor.onlyChannelsHint: Logins separated by commas. Empty = all channels.

templates.hint: A template is a complete card design: canvas, elements, colors, typefaces and animations. What you leave here is the default; each streamer can change it for their channel.
templates.keyHint: Lowercase letters, numbers, hyphen and underscore. It cannot be changed later.
templates.zone: Zone where it goes by default
templates.deleteBody: “{{name}}” will be removed. Pieces that used it are left without a template.
templates.emptyHint: Create a card or a banner and design it in the editor.

limits.title: Viewer-care limits
limits.hint: Limits so promotion does not flood the stream. Each streamer can be more discreet than this, never more insistent.
limits.minGap: Minimum seconds between two pieces in the same zone
limits.hourlyCap: Maximum seconds of promotion on screen per hour
limits.minDurationHint: No streamer can leave a piece on screen for less than this.
limits.maxDurationHint: Cap on how long they can make it.
limits.minScaleHint: 100 is the design's size. They can't shrink it below this.
limits.maxScaleHint: They can't enlarge it above this.
limits.maxMarginHint: How far the streamer can move a zone from the edge of the 1920×1080 canvas.
limits.botPerOwnHint: How many bot pieces play before each of the streamer's own cards. 1 = they alternate. With no active bot pieces, no own card plays.
limits.ownInterval: Minimum minutes between repeats of an own card
limits.ownIntervalHint: No own card can repeat more often than this, even if the streamer sets less.
limits.oneAtATime: One piece at a time across all zones
limits.oneAtATimeHint: On: while one zone shows a piece, the others wait. This keeps the overlay from overwhelming the stream, even if the streamer places two zones on top of each other. Off: each zone runs on its own.

design.canvasDescription: Drag and resize each element on the canvas. The canvas is the card: what you see is exactly what shows up in OBS.
design.noElements: This card has no elements. Add one with the buttons in the layers list.

text.templateHint: Variables: {{vars}}. If it ends up empty, the element is not shown.

qr.hint: The QR only shows if the piece has a link and the QR turned on.

design.wholeAnimationHint: It adds to each element's own: this is how the whole card comes in and goes out.
design.livePreviewHint: The card at its zone's position, as it would look on stream.

zones.hint: A zone is a place on the 1920×1080 canvas where a card goes by default. The streamer can move it afterwards.
zones.deleteBody: “{{name}}” will be removed. It can only be deleted if no piece or template uses it.

slots.title: What the streamer can change
slots.description: Each setting is a color, a fixed text or a font. Choose which elements it reaches; the streamer saves one value per setting and can go back to yours. Anything not declared here cannot be changed.
slots.empty: This template has no settings for the streamer.
slots.targetsHint: One color can drive several properties at once.
slots.noTargets: This design has no elements that accept this kind of setting.

ownCards.hint: Cards that streamers write for their own channel. Hide the ones that break the rules: the streamer still sees it, but it does not appear in their overlay.
ownCards.empty: No streamer has created own cards yet.

panel.title: Promotions
panel.subtitle: Decatron cards and banners that show up on your stream on their own, timed so they don't tire your chat.
panel.loadFailed: Couldn't load. Try again in a moment.
panel.forbidden: You need overlays permission on this channel.

guide.title: How to use it
guide.description: It's a single browser source in OBS. The server decides what shows and when; you don't have to do anything else.
guide.step1Body: Copy this link and add it as a «Browser source».
guide.obs3: Width 1920 and height 1080 (it covers the whole scene; the background is transparent).
guide.warnMixed: The all-platforms link and a single-platform one are both connected: promotions would show up twice.
guide.warnRepeated: That's fine if they're in different scenes; otherwise promotions will show twice and count double toward the hourly cap.
guide.step2Body: The «What is shown» tab lists the active pieces exactly as they appear on screen.
guide.step3Body: At least {{gap}} seconds pass between two pieces of the same zone, and never more than {{cap}} seconds of promotion per hour are shown.
guide.step4Body: Everything above in more detail, and what to check if nothing shows:

pieces.title: Active pieces
pieces.description: What Decatron can show on your channel right now. They come out by priority and, at equal priority, at random by weight.
pieces.empty: There are no published pieces yet.
pieces.off: Off: it won't show on your channel

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: You decide how much shows. You can be more discreet than Decatron, never more insistent.
settings.pauseHint: The OBS source stays connected but nothing shows until you turn it back on.
settings.gap: Pause between pieces of a zone
settings.gapHint: At least {{n}} seconds. Raise it to space them out more.
settings.capHint: At most {{n}} seconds. Lower it to see fewer promotions.
settings.saved: Saved. It applies from the next piece.

command.title: Chat command
command.description: Lets you or your team run the promos from chat, without opening the panel.
command.enableHint: It is off by default. Works on Twitch and Kick.
command.name: Command name
command.nameHint: 2 to 20 letters, numbers or underscore. It cannot match a bot command or one of your own.
command.roleHint: The streamer and the Lead Moderator always can.
command.cooldownHint: During that time the bot ignores new uses.
command.usage: Usage: !{{name}} show <name> · !{{name}} list · !{{name}} pause · !{{name}} resume. «Show» puts that piece on screen at the next chance, even if paused or if you turned it off.
command.otherBot: If you use another bot (Nightbot, StreamElements…), check it has no command with that name: it can't be detected from here.
command.cmdInvalid: The command name isn't valid: use 2 to 20 lowercase letters, numbers or underscore.
command.cmdReserved: That name is already used by a bot command. Pick another.
command.cmdCustom: You already have a custom command with that name. Pick another.

timing.title: Timing
timing.description: How many seconds each piece stays on screen. You can choose between {{min}} and {{max}} seconds.

position.title: Position
position.description: Drag each card to where you want it in your scene. You can move it away from the edge up to {{max}} pixels.

design.title: Design
design.description: Pick each piece's template and size. Size can go from {{min}}% to {{max}}%.

triggers.title: Triggers
triggers.description: Make a piece show up at specific moments of your stream, hands-free. Works on Twitch.
triggers.next: The next one in the rotation
triggers.pieceHint: Pick a piece or one of your cards, or let the next one from the normal rotation show.
triggers.delayHint: Between 0 and 120 s. Gives your audience time to arrive.

start.label: When the stream starts
start.hint: Shows once when the stream begins. If it drops and comes back within 15 minutes it does not repeat.

raid.label: After a raid
raid.hint: Shows when a raid arrives. It does not repeat if several arrive in a row (3 minutes between them).

triggers.note: Triggers respect the Promotions pause: if it is on, nothing shows. “After a break in the stream” is coming later.

stats.intro: How many times each piece appeared on your overlay. Only deliveries to the overlay are counted, with no viewer identified. Kept for 90 days.
